What makes a lizard so amazing?

The nimble lizard is an amazing reptile that drops its own tail and dashes away when in danger. The way it basks in the sun every morning is fascinating too.

content.alt: Lizard - Nature and science facts about lizards
content.text:
Nature and science facts about lizards

Because a lizard can't regulate its own body temperature (it's ectothermic), it warms up in the morning sun before becoming active. When a predator grabs it, it drops its own tail (autotomy) to escape, and the regrown tail is filled with cartilage instead of bone. It senses scent particles with its tongue, some species change their skin color to hide, and lizards lay eggs and shed their skin regularly.

Great things to observe together

Point out sun-basking (being ectothermic), tail-dropping (autotomy), skin-shedding, and camouflage. Talking together about "Why does a lizard drop its tail?" is a wonderful way to spark curiosity.

content.text:
Parent guide — how to nurture curiosity

Explain that "when it's in danger, it leaves its tail behind and runs (the tail grows back)," and compare it to how snakes shed their skin. Comparing why it basks in the sun (being ectothermic) with how humans stay warm makes it even more interesting.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. Why does a lizard drop its tail?
A. When a predator grabs it, it drops its own tail (autotomy) to escape. The tail grows back (with cartilage).

Q. Why does a lizard bask in the sun?
A. It's an ectotherm that can't regulate its own body temperature, so it warms up in the morning sun before becoming active.

Q. How can we observe lizards at home?
A. Compare it with how snakes shed their skin, and compare why it basks in the sun with how humans stay warm.
